question: Mohiniyattam dance form gets its name from Hindu God ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Vishnu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Mohiniyattam is a classical dance form from Kerala, India.
 
• **The term "Mohiniyattam" translates to "dance of the enchantress."**
 
• The dance form gets its name from the Hindu God Vishnu.
 
• In Hindu mythology, **Mohini is a female avatar of Lord Vishnu.**
 
• Mohiniyattam reflects the theme of love and devotion, **where the dancer often plays the role of Mohini, who is the amorous and devoted heroine.**
 
• **Mohini, the divine enchantress, is often depicted as seductive, beautiful, and capable of mesmerizing those who she wishes to influence.**
 
• The dance form is characterized by graceful and gentle movements, **and it is traditionally performed solo by women.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
 

 God
 Relation to Dance
 
 
 
 

 Kartikeya
 Kartikeya, also known as Murugan, is often associated with Tamil folk dance forms like "Kavadi Attam," performed in honour of him.
 
 

 Shiva
 
 
Shiva, as Nataraja, is known as the Lord of Dance.

 
The dance form Tandava symbolizes the cosmic cycles of creation and destruction, as well as the daily rhythm of birth and death.

 
One of the classical Indian dances, Bharatanatyam, draws heavily from the dance poses held by the cosmic dancer Shiva.

 
 
 

 Krishna
 Krishna, an avatar of Vishnu, is associated with the classical dance form of Kathak and the folk dance form of Raas Leela or Raas Lilas, which portray his early life, love-play with Radha, and his flirtatious interactions with the Gopis.
